Chapter 6

Exercise 4

Page 194
PROBLEM STATEMENT
Chapter 6, Page 194
Step 1

Discrete\textbf{Discrete}Discrete data are restricted to defined separated values, for example integers or counts. Continuous\textbf{Continuous}Continuous data are not restricted to defined separate values, but can occupy any value over a continuous range, for example decimal, rational or real numbers.

(a) Discrete, because the number of new accounts are counts (that is, nonnegative integers).

(b) Continuous, because the time between customer arrivals can take on decimal values (such as 2.5 minutes or 23.75 seconds).

(c) Discrete, because the number of customers are counts (that is, nonnegative integers).

(d) Continuous, because the amount of fuel can take on decimal values (such as 14.5 gallons).

(e) Discrete, because the number of minorities are counts (that is, nonnegative integers).

(f) Continuous, because the outside temperature can take on decimal values (such as 7.5°\text{\textdegree}° C).

🎯 Result

(a) Discrete

(b) Continuous

(c) Discrete

(d) Continuous

(e) Discrete

(f) Continuous

A random variable\textbf{random variable}random variable is a variable that is assigned a value at random from some set of possible values.

A probability distribution\textbf{probability distribution}probability distribution is a function that assigns a probability (value between 0 and 1) to all possible values of a random variable.

Thus we note that a probability distribution includes a probability besides the possible values of a random variable, while a random variable contains only the possible values.

🎯 Result

A probability distribution includes a probability besides the possible values of a random variable, while a random variable contains only the possible values.

Discrete\textbf{Discrete}Discrete data are restricted to defined separated values, for example integers or counts. Continuous\textbf{Continuous}Continuous data are not restricted to defined separate values, but can occupy any value over a continuous range, for example decimal, rational or real numbers.

(a) Continuous, because the length of time can take on decimal values (such as 27.5 minutes).

(b) Discrete, because the number of cars are counts (that is, nonnegative integers).

(c) Discrete, because the number of hits are counts (that is, nonnegative integers).

(d) Discrete, because the number of patients are counts (that is, nonnegative integer).

(e) Continuous, because the distance can take on decimal values (such as 7.5 miles or 9.75 kilometers).

(f) Discrete, because the number of customers are counts (that is, nonnegative integer).

(g) Continuous, because the distance can take on decimal values (such as 7.5 miles or 9.75 kilometers).

🎯 Result

(a) Continuous

(b) Discrete

(c) Discrete

(d) Discrete

(e) Continuous

(f) Discrete

(g) Continuous

(a) The mean (expected value) of a binomial distribution is the product of the sample size nnn and the probability π\piπ:

μ=nπ=15×0.67=10.05\mu=n\pi =15\times 0.67=10.05 μ=nπ=15×0.67=10.05

The standard deviation of a binomial distribution is the square root of the product of the sample size nnn and the probabilities π\piπ and 1−π1-\pi1−π (that is, the standard deviation is the square root of the variance).

σ=nπ(1−π)=15(0.67)(1−0.67)≈1.8211\sigma=\sqrt{n\pi (1-\pi )}=\sqrt{15(0.67)(1-0.67)}\approx 1.8211 σ=nπ(1−π)​=15(0.67)(1−0.67)​≈1.8211

Thus we expect 10.05 pennies, with a standard deviation of 1.8211 pennies.

DEFINITIONS

Formula Poisson probability:

P(X=k)=μke−μk!P(X=k)=\dfrac{\mu^k e^{-\mu}}{k!} P(X=k)=k!μke−μ​

Complement rule:

P(∼A)=P(not A)=1−P(A)P(\sim A)=P(\text{not }A)=1-P(A) P(∼A)=P(not A)=1−P(A)

Addition rule for disjoint or mutually exclusive events:

P(A∪B)=P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)P(A\cup B)=P(A\text{ or }B)=P(A)+P(B) P(A∪B)=P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)

Step 2

SOLUTION

The mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values:

x‾=∑i=1nxin=212+161+145+...+17230=504230≈168.0667\begin{align*} \overline{x}&=\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n} \\ &=\dfrac{\begin{matrix}212+161+145+...+172\end{matrix}}{30} \\ &=\dfrac{5042}{30} \\ &\approx 168.0667 \end{align*}x​=n∑i=1n​xi​​=30212+161+145+...+172​​=305042​≈168.0667​

We have been given that the mean of the Poisson distribution will be the sample mean divided by 162 and multiplied by 2.

μ=Mean×2162=168.0667×181≈2.0749\mu=\text{Mean}\times \frac{2}{162}=168.0667\times \frac{1}{81}\approx 2.0749 μ=Mean×1622​=168.0667×811​≈2.0749

(a) Evaluate the probability of Poisson probability at x=0x=0x=0:

P(X=0)=μke−μk!=2.07490e−2.07490!=1e−2.07491=e−2.0749≈0.1256=12.56%\begin{align*} P(X=0)&=\dfrac{\mu^k e^{-\mu}}{k!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749^0 e^{-2.0749}}{0!} \\ &=\dfrac{1 e^{-2.0749}}{1} \\ &=e^{-2.0749} \\ &\approx 0.1256 \\ &=12.56\% \end{align*}P(X=0)​=k!μke−μ​=0!2.07490e−2.0749​=11e−2.0749​=e−2.0749≈0.1256=12.56%​

Step 3

(b) Evaluate the probability of Poisson probability at x=2x=2x=2:

P(X=2)=μke−μk!=2.07492e−2.07492!=2.07492e−2.07492≈0.2703=27.03%\begin{align*} P(X=2)&=\dfrac{\mu^k e^{-\mu}}{k!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749^2 e^{-2.0749}}{2!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749^2 e^{-2.0749}}{2} \\ &\approx 0.2703 \\ &=27.03\% \end{align*}P(X=2)​=k!μke−μ​=2!2.07492e−2.0749​=22.07492e−2.0749​≈0.2703=27.03%​

(c) Evaluate the probability of Poisson probability at x=1,3x=1,3x=1,3:

P(X=1)=μke−μk!=2.07491e−2.07491!=2.0749e−2.07491=2.0749e−2.0749≈0.2605P(X=3)=μke−μk!=2.07493e−2.07493!=2.07493e−2.07496≈0.1869\begin{align*} P(X=1)&=\dfrac{\mu^k e^{-\mu}}{k!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749^1 e^{-2.0749}}{1!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749 e^{-2.0749}}{1} \\ &=2.0749 e^{-2.0749} \\ &\approx 0.2605 \\ P(X=3)&=\dfrac{\mu^k e^{-\mu}}{k!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749^3 e^{-2.0749}}{3!} \\ &=\dfrac{2.0749^3 e^{-2.0749}}{6} \\ &\approx 0.1869 \end{align*}P(X=1)P(X=3)​=k!μke−μ​=1!2.07491e−2.0749​=12.0749e−2.0749​=2.0749e−2.0749≈0.2605=k!μke−μ​=3!2.07493e−2.0749​=62.07493e−2.0749​≈0.1869​
